page: Microsoft Azure E2s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv7 server family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration includes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, supported by a large 480 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, though it is premium storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The E2s_v7 demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, placing in the top 10% of Geekbench single-core tests and showing strong single-threaded compression and decompression speeds. Conversely, multi-core performance is weak, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks placing in the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. Memory bandwidth tests also show lower efficiency, particularly for large uncached read and write operations.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E2s_v7 provides a dense memory profile relative to its low vCPU count. This makes it an efficient choice for workloads that are constrained by memory capacity rather than parallel processing power, allowing users to avoid paying for unneeded CPU cores. The lack of bundled local storage and GPU accelerators further streamlines the hardware profile for pure memory-bound tasks.

The Microsoft Azure E2s_v7 is best suited for memory-intensive, single-threaded, or lightly threaded applications. Recommended workloads include caching layers, lightweight database operations, text processing, and basic web serving where high memory capacity and strong single-core execution are prioritized over multi-threaded throughput.
